en.title: James Gunn Clarifies Skydance's Involvement with 'Man of Tomorrow'
en.summary: Rumors swirled that Skydance executives were concerned about the quality of the upcoming 'Superman' sequel, 'Man of Tomorrow.' Director James Gunn has now stepped in to set the record straight.
en.body:
The superhero landscape is constantly abuzz with whispers and rumors, especially when a major creative shift occurs. Following his departure as co-head of DC Studios, director **James Gunn** found himself addressing a particularly persistent piece of online chatter concerning the upcoming **Superman** sequel, tentatively titled **'Man of Tomorrow.'** The speculation suggested that executives at **Skydance**, the new parent company of Warner Bros., had seen the film and were so concerned about its quality that it fueled Gunn's exit.

However, **Gunn** took to the social platform Threads to definitively debunk these claims. He clarified that the narrative of Skydance executives reviewing the film and planning drastic changes is entirely false. According to **Gunn**, the only individuals who have seen **'Man of Tomorrow'** are his DC Studios partner **Peter Safran** and a very select group of close friends and family. This direct refutation aims to quell the rising tide of misinformation that often accompanies high-profile projects.

## Clearing the Air on 'Man of Tomorrow'

The rumor mill had been churning with allegations that **Skydance** was unhappy with the early cuts of **'Man of Tomorrow,'** even going so far as to suggest the film might be relegated to streaming or face significant reshoots. This, the rumors implied, was a contributing factor to **Gunn** and **Safran** stepping down from their leadership roles at DC Studios after a four-year tenure. **Gunn's** statement directly counters this, emphasizing that the film's alleged issues with **Skydance** simply never happened.

> "No one from Skydance has even seen the movie — the only people that have are Peter Safran and a very small trusted group of friends and family." — **James Gunn**

This clarification is crucial for fans who are eager to see **David Corenswet** don the iconic cape. The narrative of internal conflict or creative disagreements at this stage could cast a shadow over the highly anticipated film. By providing a clear statement, **Gunn** allows the focus to return to the film itself and its intended release.

## What This Means for the Man of Steel

For dedicated fans of **Superman** and the evolving DC Universe, **Gunn's** clarification is a breath of fresh air. The constant speculation can be exhausting, and knowing that the film is proceeding without major external creative interference from a new corporate entity offers a sense of stability. It suggests that the vision for **'Man of Tomorrow'** remains intact, at least from the perspective of those closest to its production. The fact that **Skydance** hasn't even viewed the film yet indicates that the rumors were baseless, likely stemming from the broader corporate restructuring happening around Warner Bros.

## What's Next

**'Man of Tomorrow'** is currently slated for a theatrical release on July 9, 2027. Further details regarding its marketing campaign and any potential early screenings for press or industry professionals have not yet been announced.
